subject: CURRENT-DATE function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. The prior verdict rested on TWO edges it called unverified; I executed BOTH against the shipping binary, so its stated basis no longer holds - one edge is CORRECT and the other emits a value 15.21.3 forbids, with no conforming alternative available in the standard, which is an owner call, not a mechanical fix. Citation re-run: cite.py --check 15.21.3 'The character positions returned, numbered from left to right' OK (rule 1, Returned value rule); 7.3.17.4 GR2 'the implementor defines whether a value greater than 59 may be reported' OK. PATH READ: IntrinsicRenderer#RenderString maps "CurrentDate" to RuntimeApi.DateFn with an empty argument list; CobolDate#CurrentDate is Format21(RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now()) (it read DateTimeOffset.Now when this path was first walked; R21 moved it onto the seam); CobolDate#Format21 is t.ToString("yyyyMMddHHmmssff", InvariantCulture) + (t.Offset >= TimeSpan.Zero ? "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00"). InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits (positions 1-4). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, COBOL side: 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD' (PIC X(21)) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 -> '2026073010404830-0700'; FUNCTION LENGTH of the function = 0021. Receiver varied per the PB5 lesson - PIC X(30) space-pads to '...-0700         ', PIC X(8) truncates to '20260730', PIC N(21) carries all 21, and STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE contributes exactly 21 characters - so no receiver scale hides a layout defect. VERIFIED BY DIRECT EXECUTION OF THE SHIPPING METHOD (loaded src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime.dll and invoked WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime.CobolDate.Format21 over fixed DateTimeOffsets, since TimeZoneInfo.Local reads the Windows registry and ignores TZ): +05:45 -> '2026073010331564+0545', -09:30 -> '...-0930', +12:45 -> '...+1245', 00:00 -> '...+0000', -12:00 -> '...-1200', +13:00 -> '...+1300'. So positions 20-21 (the prior pass's unverified edge (b)) are CORRECT for non-zero minute offsets, position 17 is correct on BOTH branches including the 'same as UTC' => '+' boundary, and the '-' branch reaches -14:00 too - CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 'cannot exceed 12 because no TimeZoneInfo zone is below -12:00', which is true of the HOST ZONE TABLE and false of the value CURRENT-DATE reports: WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK pins a DateTimeOffset directly and that type admits -14:00, so the departure is symmetric and the documentation names both signs. THE ONE OPEN POINT, now demonstrated rather than suspected: +14:00 -> '2026073010331564+1400'. 15.21.3 positions 18-19 state 'If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13', and Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) is UNCLAMPED, so a run on a host whose TimeZoneInfo.Local is 'Line Islands Standard Time' / Pacific-Kiritimati (UTC+14, a zone Windows and IANA both ship) returns '14' there. The reason this is NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION and not DIVERGES: the standard's table offers NO in-range value for a +14 host, so no behavior conforms - emitting 14 (today) is an out-of-range implementor extension, clamping to 13 misreports the offset, and returning '0'/'00'/'00' means 'the system has no facility to provide the local time differential factor', which is false. Nothing in CobolDate.cs, docs/CONFORMANCE.md or the design docs records a decision, and the same unclamped expression also feeds WHEN-COMPILED (15.99.3, identical table). THE BARE OWNER QUESTION: on a host whose local UTC offset is +14:00, what shall CURRENT-DATE (and WHEN-COMPILED) return in character positions 17-19? CORRECTED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD: positions 13-14 do conform without qualification - 7.3.17.4 GR1 implies OFF when no LEAP-SECOND directive is written and GR3 then forbids >59, which .NET's 'ss' can never emit; GR2's ON case leaves >59 to the implementor, so ignoring the directive (it sits in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.KnownIgnoredDirectives) is conforming on both branches, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md's 'documented non-support' wording for >>LEAP-SECOND overstates the exposure for THIS rule. CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (the sentence this replaces was written before R21 and asserted the opposite): CurrentDate() reads the INJECTABLE seam - CobolDate.cs 'public static string CurrentDate() => Format21(RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now())' - so CURRENT-DATE, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE and the windowing defaults observe ONE clock per run unit, the §15.100.3 r5 YEAR-TO-YYYY identity holds, and ClockSeamDriftTests is the source-form guard that no direct DateTime[Offset].Now read comes back. test-needed: (i) a unit test over CobolDate.Format21 with fixed DateTimeOffsets (+14:00, +13:00, -12:00, +05:45, -09:30, a zero-hundredths instant, a single-digit month/day) asserting every position's 15.21.3 range, and (ii) a conformance case pinning CURRENT-DATE through the injectable clock once that seam covers it. The only existing spec-derived test touching CURRENT-DATE (IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec, verified on disk) asserts only the ordering CURRENT-DATE >= WHEN-COMPILED and inspects NO character position of the CURRENT-DATE value, so it does not cover this rule and test-ref stays empty. || OWNER DETERMINATION RECORDED 2026-08-30 (answered via AskUserQuestion: "True offset"); NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -> DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT. THE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED: on a host whose local UTC offset lies outside the rule's table, CURRENT-DATE and WHEN-COMPILED REPORT THE TRUE OFFSET. ONE DETERMINATION, BOTH ROWS: RV-15.21.3-1 and RV-15.99.3-1 share it because one formatter serves both (CobolDate.Format21) and §15.99.3 r1's table is character-for-character §15.21.3 r1's; the compile-time bake (IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock) and the run-time read (RunUnit.Current.Clock) are independent seams onto that one formatter, and the shared test asserts they agree rather than assuming it. WHY NO ALTERNATIVE CONFORMS: the rule caps positions 18-19 at 00..13 under '+' and 00..12 under '-' (cite.py --check 15.21.3 'two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13 indicating the number of hours that the local time is ahead of Coordinated Universal Time' -> OK; the same text --check'd against 15.99.3 -> OK), and for a +14:00 host the table names no value at all - emitting 14 leaves the range, clamping to 13 misreports what §15.21.1 defines as 'the ... local time differential factor provided by the system on which the function is evaluated' (--check -> OK), and '0'/'00'/'00' asserts position 17's 'the system ... does not have the facility to provide the local time differential factor' (--check 15.21.3 -> OK), which is false. Reporting the truth is the only option that states nothing untrue. DOCUMENTED per §4.2.6 ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK) and §4.2.7 (--check 'Language elements that an implementor may, but need not, implement are listed in A.4' -> OK), in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 as a named determination bullet. BOTH SIGNS, and the '+' one is a real host: IANA Pacific/Kiritimati = Windows 'Line Islands Standard Time' ('(UTC+14:00) Kiritimati Island' - read off the host zone table, not inherited); the '-' side is unreachable from any host zone but reachable through the WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK pin, which parses a DateTimeOffset directly and so admits -14:00. THE DEPARTURE IS BOUNDED, AND THE TEST PINS THE BOUND: CurrentDateOffsetDeterminationTests re-derives the whole §15.21.3 r1 position table from the rule text and requires the set of out-of-range position spans to be EXACTLY {18-19} across the fixtures and EMPTY for every offset the rule admits - so a regression that broke positions 15-16 or 20-21 at an extreme offset fails even while the headline value still looks right. End to end through the clock seam: CurrentDateOffsetPinTests runs a COBOL program under WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK at +14:00, -14:00, +13:00, +05:45, +00:00 and -09:30 and asserts all 21 characters.
